_about: Debug Knowledge Pack — curated, offline mapping of failure MECHANISMS to real Intel debug wiki pages, BIOS/firmware code areas, and concrete next steps. Grounded in BIOSBKM Debug CookBook, DebugEncyclopedia, and BIOS FAS/HAS spec content. Extensible: add entries freely. Each entry: match[] keywords (any hit triggers it), title, summary, wiki_links[], code_paths[], debug_steps[].

entries.title: UPI/KTI topology-failover / port-disable system hang (socket removed, S3M, check-in)
entries.summary: After a degraded/disabled UPI link, BIOS (UPIRC) forces the platform into a supported topology (2S-6L -> 2S-4L -> 1S), removing the remote socket. Hang occurs if BIOS still waits for the removed socket to set its check-in bit, or if S3M socket-removal updated one bitmap but not all consumers, so the SBSP waits indefinitely.
wiki_links: BIOSBKM Debug CookBook (soft vs hard hang, itp.halt/go, MCA/Pcode capture): https://wiki.ith.intel.com/display/BIOSBKM/Debug+CookBook
code_paths: MultiSocketLib.c — SBSP/AP minimum-path topology calculation & disabled-link handling
UPI Reference Code (UPIRC) — topology discovery, degraded-topology forcing, deadlock-free routing
S3M socket-removal — socket-present / active-socket / adjacency / AP-startup / routing bitmaps
SBSP check-in handshake — BOOT_GO via remote Scratchpad1; wait for check-in via remote Scratchpad2
debug_steps: Classify the hang: run itp.halt() — if IA halts it's a SOFT hang (itp.go() to resume); check keyboard LEDs (NumLock/CapsLock toggle => alive). No response/power button dead => HARD hang: connect ITP, unlock, capture PMC/MCA/Pcode/core-live.

Capture topology before vs after failover: expected topology, detected-before-degrade, after port-disable, socket-present bitmap, socket-removed bitmap (esp. S3M-driven), SBSP chosen socket, AP enumeration, MultiSocketLib path result.

Validate S3M socket-removal is CONSISTENT across ALL structures: socket-present map, active-socket map, UPI/KTI adjacency matrix, AP startup list, SBSP routing table, MultiSocketLib path DB, and the check-in/rendezvous bitmap. A stale entry in any one causes the hang.

Check the SBSP<->AP check-in handshake: SBSP issues BOOT_GO on the remote socket's non-sticky Scratchpad1 and waits for the check-in bit on Scratchpad2. If the socket was removed but BIOS still waits, the SBSP hangs until timeout -> appears as a 2S boot hang.
Read BIOSSCRATCHPAD7 progress/check-in state when hung and correlate with which socket/AP failed to check in.

entries.title: Machine Check (MCA) decode — bus/interconnect (UPI/IIO) class
entries.summary: MCi_STATUS with MCACOD 0x0800-class indicates a bus/interconnect error (UPI/QPI/IIO). Decode the architectural bits (VAL/OVER/UC/PCC), MCACOD (15:0) and MSCOD (31:16), then map the bank to the failing IP.
wiki_links: BIOSBKM Debug CookBook — MCA capture on hang: https://wiki.ith.intel.com/display/BIOSBKM/Debug+CookBook
code_paths: MCA bank status registers (MCi_STATUS / MCi_ADDR / MCi_MISC) per socket/uncore
IP-specific MSCOD decode — see the failing IP's MCA spec
debug_steps: Decode MCi_STATUS: bits 63..55 = VAL/OVER/UC/EN/MISCV/ADDRV/PCC/S/AR; MCACOD = bits 15:0; MSCOD = bits 31:16.
MCACOD 0x0800-class => bus/interconnect (UPI/QPI/IIO). Identify the bank number to locate the failing unit.
sv.socket<N>.uncore.mca_bank<B>.status.read() then decode; read MCi_ADDR/MCi_MISC for the address/context.
Correlate RIP + bank to the IP; use MSCOD against that IP's MCA spec for the model-specific cause.

entries.title: UPI/KTI link error / retrain / CRC
entries.summary: UPI link CRC errors, retrains, or failed training. Distinguish physical link-integrity issues from protocol/transaction issues.
code_paths: UPIRC link training / PHY (c_init_begin, L1 forcing)
KTI PHY status registers (ktilk_ph_ctr_status, KTICRCERRCNT_REG, KTIPH_RXL0C_ERR_STS_REG)
debug_steps: Read UPI link status per port: sv.socket<N>.upi.upi<port>.ktilk_ph_ctr_status.read() (confirm exact reg via tab-complete).
If CRC/retry counters are set -> link-integrity path (marginal PHY / training params). Else -> protocol/transaction path.
Compare training params/timing across passing vs failing FW/ucode releases (e.g. UPLR regression).

entries.title: Boot hang / POST checkpoint stall
entries.summary: System stalls at a POST checkpoint. The last good checkpoint localizes the failing BIOS phase; inspect the code path immediately after it.
code_paths: PEI/DXE phase modules around the last checkpoint
debug_steps: Find the last successful POST/major checkpoint before the hang in the serial/BIOS log.
Read BIOSSCRATCHPAD progress registers to confirm the phase; inspect the module executed right after.
Classify soft vs hard hang (itp.halt) and capture MCA/Pcode/PMC state.

entries.title: Memory training / ECC (DDR/DIMM)
entries.summary: Memory training failure or ECC (CE/UE) errors. Localize to channel/rank/DIMM and correlate the address.
debug_steps: Grep the MRC/BIOS log for the failing training step + channel/rank; capture DIMM SPD/config.
Correlate CE/UE address to channel/rank/bank; check DfxPoisonEn and mcelog thresholds.

entries.title: CPU straps / soft-strap misconfiguration
entries.summary: Incorrect CPU straps (soft-straps) can cause boot hangs that vanish once the straps are corrected (a common no-repro closure cause).
debug_steps: Dump straps: sv.socket<N>.io<N>.uncore.hwrs.gpsb.poc_straps.show().
Compare against the known-good strap configuration for the SKU/QDF; correct and re-test.
If setting straps resolves it -> strap/provisioning issue, not silicon (often closed as no-repro).
